failedAssertions.reason: Guard code IS present in App.tsx:69-73 and works after page reload, but FAILS in the normal user flow (Settings > enable proxy > navigate to validation > Start). Root cause: useSettings() is a custom hook with useState, not a shared React Context. Each component that calls useSettings() gets independent state. When user enables proxy in SettingsContent, only that component's React state and localStorage are updated. App component's React state (which contains handleStartValidation) still has proxy.enabled=false. After page reload, App's useEffect reads updated localStorage and the guard works. Fix needed: either convert useSettings to a React Context/Provider pattern for shared state, or have handleStartValidation read directly from localStorage (via getProxyFromStorage() or localStorage.getItem) instead of relying on React state.
failedAssertions.suggestedFix: Option A (quick fix): In handleStartValidation (App.tsx:66), replace the check on settings.proxy.enabled with a direct localStorage read: `const proxySettings = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('proxy-settings') || '{}'); if (proxySettings.enabled && (!proxySettings.proxies || proxySettings.proxies.length === 0)) { ... }`. Option B (proper fix): Convert useSettings to use React.createContext/useContext Provider pattern so all components share the same state instance.
